title: Known-key · multiple differential trails

target.description: 7-round standard AES; initial whitening and omitted final MixColumns per Section2. Multiple-differential core and Gilbert boundary extension.

setting.key_relation: One public standard AES master key. Verifier witness offsets are existential and need not equal its actual round keys.
setting.key_population: General standard AES keys, supplied to the shortcut player
setting.plaintext_model: One distinct input/output pair-of-pairs with input difference in some diagonal subspace D_j and output difference in some mixed subspace M_l. The indices j,l are free.
assumptions: Classical known-key relation directly on the input/output difference spaces. No AES key-schedule constraint is imposed on the existential boundary offsets. Case1: the generic reference counts permutation/inverse oracle queries; the shortcut budget includes tuple generation and verifier work.
The source does not prove that the proposed generic-player strategy is optimal; Section12 leaves that question open.
setting.reference_model: Classical known-key relation directly on the input/output difference spaces. No AES key-schedule constraint is imposed on the existential boundary offsets. Case1: the generic reference counts permutation/inverse oracle queries; the shortcut budget includes tuple generation and verifier work.

time.note: Tuple-generation plus verifier costs under the same n. Source Table2 verifier normalization is retained.

data.note: Output witnesses generated by the public-cipher algorithm; not secret-key data queries.

memory.note: Table1/Table2 memory exponent; no uniform entry-width conversion is asserted.

preprocessing.note: Rebound/key-filter setup is retained within the source total estimate; no separate reusable setup amount is stated.

success.description: The source states construction costs and qualitative success or expected tuple generation, without a numerical fixed-budget shortcut-player success law.

review.scope: PDF p.5 Table1; pp.50–51 AppendixE.1/Figure6 and source known-key definitions pp.10–12. Primary shortcut output event checked separately from generic-player probabilities.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5 Table1; pp.50–51 AppendixE.1/Figure6 and source known-key definitions pp.10–12.
evidence.interpretation: Defining primary-text costs, output event and conditions checked together.

limitations: The result is a known-key witness construction, not secret-key recovery.
The original source model and generic-reference cost case are retained.
